chosen.title: Data Centers in Orbit: Why Big Tech Wants to Move AI's Power Problem to Space
chosen.rationale: The race to build orbital data centers is accelerating right now as hyperscalers hit a power wall on Earth (Rubin-class GPU racks pushing toward 300kW-1MW each) — it's the exact intersection of Kenji's aerospace obsession and AI infrastructure beat, and nobody in the AIMA archive has covered the space angle on the compute crunch (the existing 'Power Hungry' piece is ground-based carbon accounting only).

sources.name: Bloomberg — The Race to Rethink Data Centers for AI's Power Surge

rejected_candidates.title: The Machine That Called the Hurricane: Inside AI's New Disaster-Prediction Models
rejected_candidates.rationale: Google DeepMind's model nailing both the path and Category 5 intensity of Hurricane Melissa, plus USC's real-time wildfire-ignition model published this year, is a live, scored, verifiable AI-does-something-real story with immediate stakes — squarely Kenji's 'mechanism + honest reckoning' structure (who gets the warning, who doesn't) and his climate-tech beat.

sources.name: MIT Technology Review — Three climate technologies breaking through in 2026

rejected_candidates.title: The Robot That Outran Us: What a Marathon-Winning Humanoid Actually Proves
rejected_candidates.rationale: A fully autonomous humanoid beating the human half-marathon world record by nearly 7 minutes, landing the same season NVIDIA ships a dedicated safety architecture for physical AI, is a vivid 'moment of contact' scene made for Kenji — and it's a distinct angle from AIMA's already-published IPO and factory-floor humanoid pieces (endurance/locomotion + safety governance, not markets or manufacturing).

sources.name: Robot Magazine — Why 2026 could be the pivotal year for Humanoid Robots
